title: Clear shifts keeps ended shifts, removes future ones, trims a running one
custom_preconds:
1. Sign in to the Work Orders build under test as a user whose role has Work Orders view and Work Orders create and edit. To check: Settings > Roles & Permissions > open the role > Work Orders (an Owner or Admin role has both).
  2. Use a desktop browser window at least 1024 px wide. Narrower windows show only the List, without the display switcher.
  3. In the top bar, pick the location you will test in (e.g. "Heavy Duty") and stay in it for the whole case.
  4. At least 2 technicians are eligible at this location (e.g. "Esther Howard", "Dana Ortiz"). A staff member is eligible when Clockable is on, the staff record is Active, the role is neither Office nor Time Clock User, and they are enrolled at this location. To add one:
    • Settings > Staff > add a staff member, enter a first and last name (e.g. "Dana Ortiz") and an email.
    • Pick a role that is not Office or Time Clock User (e.g. "Technician"), turn Clockable on, keep the record Active, enrol the staff member at this location, then Save.
  5. Create a customer used only by this case so a search shows only its work orders: Customers > New Customer, name (e.g. "ZZ Board Test Co"), add an asset with a unit number and year/make/model (e.g. unit "TRK-118", "2022 Freightliner M2"), then Save.
  6. Create the work order: Work Orders > New Work Order > pick the case customer (e.g. "ZZ Board Test Co") and its asset > create it, and write down its number (e.g. "S1-702").
    • On the work order page set Lead Technician to "Esther Howard".
    • On the Lines tab click New Line, enter a name (e.g. "Brake inspection") and labor hours (e.g. 2.0), and save the line.
    • Click the line's Approve (check) button so the work order status reads Approved.
  7. On the Schedule, give "Esther Howard" a shift on this work order yesterday 8:00–12:00 (already ended): Schedule > go to that day > drag the work order from the work order list onto Esther Howard's row at the start time > in the picker choose Entire work order > set the end time > save.
  8. On the Schedule, give "Esther Howard" a shift on this work order tomorrow 8:00–12:00 (not started): Schedule > go to that day > drag the work order from the work order list onto Esther Howard's row at the start time > in the picker choose Entire work order > set the end time > save.
  9. On the Schedule, give "Esther Howard" a shift on this work order today, starting 1 hour before you run the test and ending 2 hours after (e.g. 9:00–12:00 when you test at 10:00): Schedule > go to that day > drag the work order from the work order list onto Esther Howard's row at the start time > in the picker choose Entire work order > set the end time > save.
custom_steps:
1. Open Work Orders, click the All tab and pick Board View in the display switcher (right side of the toolbar; in the design its button tooltip reads "Board").
  2. Type the case customer's name (e.g. "ZZ Board Test Co") in Search.
  3. Note the exact time on your clock (e.g. 10:00).
  4. Drag the card from Esther Howard's column into Dana Ortiz's column.
  5. In the prompt click Clear shifts.
  6. Open the Schedule and read Esther Howard's shifts on this work order for yesterday, today and tomorrow.
custom_expected:
Expected results

  • Yesterday's 8:00–12:00 shift is unchanged.
  • Tomorrow's 8:00–12:00 shift is gone.
  • Today's shift now ends at the time of the change: e.g. 9:00–12:00 now reads 9:00–10:00 (3 hours before, 1 hour after). The part already under way stays on the Schedule and the rest is removed, just as Jeremy's 8:00–12:00 shift becomes 8:00–10:00 when the lead changes to Dana at 10:00.

Source — where this behaviour comes from
Epic SV-10043; story SV-10047 (Story 4, Reassign or unassign the lead technician); PRD Confluence 845185030, edited 7 Oct 2026 (status line "PRD v33"), S4-R25, read 8 Oct 2026. Review Decisions DR-38. Tech plan §12.2 item 12 still says a running shift is deleted whole; the PRD (trim) is followed. Source-verified 8 October 2026; not yet build-verified.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

  • S4-R25: “When the user chooses to clear shifts: a shift that has already ended stays as it is; a shift that has not started yet is removed; a shift that is under way at the moment of the lead change is ended at that moment, so the part already under way stays on the schedule and the rest is removed. Example: Jeremy’s shift runs 8:00 to 12:00 and the lead changes to Dana at 10:00; Jeremy’s shift now runs 8:00 to 10:00.”
